newsitem.title: USA: Boeing, McDonnell Douglas report strong profits.
newsitem.headline: Boeing, McDonnell Douglas report strong profits.

text.p: Boeing Co., the world's largest aircraft maker, and McDonnell Douglas Corp., which it agreed to buy last month, Thursday reported strong earnings for the latest quarter.
McDonnell, for which Boeing is paying $13.3 billion, said its income set records for both the fourth quarter and the year.
Boeing said it earned $254 million in the fourth quarter, up from $218 million a year earlier. Its results included income and revenue from Rockwell Corp., which was acquired Dec. 6.
The improved earnings, equal to 75 cents a share, came on revenue of $6.51 billion. A year earlier, Boeing earned 63 cents a share on sales of $4.5 billion.

Boeing attributed the increase in its earnings to higher sales volume, although the company said that was offset in part by a higher tax rate. The 1995 period also included the effects of a 10-week strike.
The 1996 period included a charge of $84 million, or 21 cents a share, to fund an employee benefit trust.
Wall Street analysts had expected Boeing to report profits equal to 99 cents a share, according to First Call, which tracks brokerage earnings estimates.
For the year, Boeing earned $1.10 billion, or $3.19 a share, on sales of $22.68 billion. In 1995, the company earned $393 million, or $1.15 a share, on sales of $19.52 billion.
The Seattle-based company's 1995 income included a charge of $254 million, or 75 cents a share, to pay for a special retirment programme.
Boeing Chairman Phil Condit said the company concluded the year with 717 new announced commercial airplane orders worth approximately $53 billion.

McDonnell Douglas said it earned $207 million, or 98 cents a share, on sales of $4.09 billion in the fourth quarter. A year earlier, the St. Louis-based company lost $936 million, or $4.18 a share, on sales of $3.73 billion.
The quarterly profits were slightly below the $1.03 per share Wall Street had anticipated, according to First Call.
For the year, McDonnell Douglas earned $788 million, or $3.64 a share, on sales of $13.83 billion. In 1995, the company lost $416 million, or $1.83 a share, on $14.33 billion in sales.

The 1995 fourth quarter and full-year results included a one-time charge related to a change in accounting procedures for its MD11 aircraft. Without the charge, fourth-quarter 1995 income would have been $187 million, or 84 cents a share, and its full-year income would have been $707 million, or $3.12 a share.
Harry C. Stonecipher, McDonnell's president, said the record 1996 performance was paced by continued strong results in the company's military aircraft business.
